sections.h2: What Is Gum Disease & Why Does It Matter?
body: Gum disease (periodontal disease) is a bacterial infection of the gum tissue and bone that supports your teeth. It begins as gingivitis — mild gum inflammation — and progresses to periodontitis, a serious condition that destroys the bone and tissue holding your teeth in place.

Nearly 47% of adults over 30 in the United States have some form of periodontal disease, making it one of the most prevalent chronic conditions in adults. Despite this, many people are unaware they have it — because early gum disease is often painless.

The consequences of untreated gum disease extend far beyond your mouth. Research has established strong links between periodontal disease and serious systemic health conditions including heart disease, stroke, type 2 diabetes, respiratory disease, and adverse pregnancy outcomes. Treating gum disease is an investment in your whole-body health — not just your smile.
Gum disease is the #1 cause of tooth loss in adults. Most cases are preventable or treatable when caught early. Don't wait for pain — many people have advanced gum disease without realising it.

body: Gum disease often progresses silently in its early stages. By the time you notice obvious symptoms, the disease may have already caused significant damage. If you're experiencing any of the following, contact us right away — early treatment is far simpler and more effective than treating advanced disease.
bullets: Gums that bleed when brushing or flossing — bleeding gums are never normal. This is the most common early sign of gingivitis, inflammation caused by bacterial build-up along the gum line.
Red, swollen, or tender gums — healthy gums should be firm and pale pink. Red, puffy, or sensitive gum tissue indicates active infection and inflammation that needs professional treatment.
Persistent bad breath (halitosis) — chronic bad breath that doesn't resolve with brushing is often caused by the bacteria colonies living below the gum line in periodontal pockets.
Receding gums — teeth look longer. As gum disease destroys supporting tissue, the gum line recedes, exposing more of the tooth root and creating sensitivity to hot and cold temperatures.
Loose or shifting teeth — advanced periodontitis destroys the bone that anchors your teeth. Loose or moving teeth in adults is a serious sign of significant bone loss requiring urgent treatment.
Gaps or changes between teeth — new spaces appearing between teeth, or a change in how your teeth fit together when you bite, can indicate shifting caused by periodontal bone loss.
Smoking & tobacco use — doubles or triples gum disease risk
Diabetes — impairs infection-fighting ability
Genetics — up to 30% higher susceptibility
Certain medications — can cause gum overgrowth or dryness
Stress — weakens immune response to bacteria
Infrequent cleanings — allows tartar build-up below gum line

sections.h2: The Three Stages of Gum Disease
body: Gum disease progresses in stages. The earlier it's treated, the simpler, less invasive, and more effective the treatment. Don't let it advance.

Stage 1 — Gingivitis: The earliest and most reversible form of gum disease. Bacteria build up in plaque irritates the gum tissue, causing inflammation. At this stage, the bone and connective tissue have not yet been affected. Gums bleed when brushing and appear red or swollen, but there is no bone loss yet — it is often completely reversible, with an excellent prognosis with treatment.

Stage 2 — Early to Moderate Periodontitis: Infection spreads below the gum line. Pockets deepen between teeth and gums (3–5mm), creating sheltered spaces for bacteria to multiply. The bone and fibers supporting your teeth begin to be destroyed, with a receding gum line, early bone loss detectable on X-rays, and persistent bad breath. Professional treatment is essential — laser therapy is highly effective at this stage.

Stage 3 — Advanced Periodontitis: Severe destruction of the bone, gum, and connective tissue that anchors your teeth, with deep pockets (6mm or more) and significant bone loss. Teeth may become loose, shift position, or require extraction, and systemic health risks are significantly elevated at this stage. Urgent treatment is required.
Not sure what stage you're at? The only way to know is a professional examination. Dr. Brown will assess your gum health, measure pocket depths, and recommend the most appropriate treatment.

sections.h2: How Gum Disease Laser Therapy Works
body: Unlike traditional periodontal surgery — which requires cutting the gum tissue with a scalpel, deep cleaning, and stitches — laser gum therapy uses a precisely calibrated laser beam delivered through a thin fibre inserted gently into the gum pocket.

The laser energy has a specific wavelength that is selectively absorbed by the diseased tissue and bacteria, while leaving healthy tissue intact. As it removes the infection, it simultaneously seals the blood vessels and stimulates the body's natural healing and bone regeneration processes.
FDA-cleared technology. Dental laser therapy for periodontal treatment has received FDA clearance and is endorsed by the American Academy of Periodontology for treating gum disease.
bullets: No scalpel required in most cases — less bleeding and swelling

Seals as it treats — reduced bleeding and faster healing

Minimal downtime — most patients return to normal activities same day

sections.h2: Laser Therapy vs. Traditional Periodontal Surgery
body: Not all gum disease treatments are equal. See how laser therapy compares to conventional surgical approaches.

Not every patient is a candidate for laser therapy alone. Dr. Brown will evaluate your specific condition and recommend the most effective treatment — which may include laser therapy, traditional scaling and root planing, or a combination approach for best results.
bullets: Scalpel required: No with laser therapy — yes with traditional surgery
Sutures (stitches): rarely needed with laser — usually required with surgery
Recovery time: same day / 24–48 hrs with laser — several days to weeks with surgery
Discomfort level: minimal with local anaesthesia — moderate to significant with surgery
Bleeding: minimal, the laser seals tissue — more significant with surgery
Healthy tissue preserved: yes, precision targeting — some healthy tissue removed in surgery
Bone regeneration potential: laser stimulates regeneration — limited with surgery
Antibacterial effect: laser destroys bacteria on contact — surgery is mechanical removal only
Anaesthesia required: local only for laser — local or general for surgery

sections.h2: Your Gum Disease Laser Treatment — Step by Step
body: We've designed the entire experience to be as comfortable, transparent, and stress-free as possible.
bullets: Comprehensive Periodontal Exam — Dr. Brown measures your gum pocket depths, reviews digital X-rays, and assesses the severity of disease. A personalised treatment plan is created and fully explained before anything begins.

Preparation & Anaesthesia — local anaesthesia is applied to ensure complete comfort throughout the procedure. In many cases, a thorough cleaning (scaling and root planing) is performed before laser treatment for optimal results.

Laser Therapy Treatment — a thin laser fiber is gently inserted into each gum pocket. The laser precisely removes infected tissue and bacteria, seals blood vessels, and stimulates the healing process. Most sessions take 1–2 hours.

Recovery & Maintenance — most patients return to normal activity within 24 hours. We provide full aftercare instructions and schedule you for periodontal maintenance visits every 3–4 months to maintain your results long-term.

faqs.q: What is gum disease laser therapy?
faqs.a: Gum disease laser therapy is a minimally invasive treatment that uses a precisely calibrated dental laser to remove infected gum tissue and bacteria from periodontal pockets. A thin laser fiber is gently inserted into the pocket, where the laser energy selectively destroys diseased tissue and bacteria while leaving healthy tissue intact. The laser simultaneously seals blood vessels, reduces bleeding, and stimulates the body's natural healing and bone regeneration processes. Unlike traditional periodontal surgery, laser therapy typically requires no scalpel and no stitches, has minimal post-treatment discomfort, and most patients return to normal activities the same day or within 24 hours.

faqs.q: Is gum disease laser therapy painful?
faqs.a: Most patients find laser gum therapy significantly more comfortable than traditional periodontal surgery. Local anaesthesia is applied before treatment begins to ensure you feel no pain during the procedure. Post-treatment discomfort is generally mild — most patients describe it as minimal soreness that resolves within a day or two. Over-the-counter pain relievers are usually sufficient if any discomfort occurs. Dr. Brown will provide specific aftercare instructions to ensure your recovery is as smooth as possible.

faqs.q: How many treatment sessions will I need?
faqs.a: The number of sessions depends on the severity and extent of your gum disease. For mild to moderate periodontitis, treatment may be completed in one to two visits. More extensive or advanced disease may require additional sessions, often divided by quadrant (one section of the mouth per visit). Following active treatment, most patients transition to periodontal maintenance visits every 3–4 months (rather than the standard 6-month interval) to monitor healing and prevent recurrence. Dr. Brown will outline your specific treatment and maintenance plan at your consultation.

faqs.q: Is laser gum treatment covered by dental insurance?
faqs.a: Many dental insurance plans cover periodontal (gum disease) treatment because it is considered medically necessary. Coverage for laser therapy specifically varies by plan — some insurers cover it at the same rate as conventional treatment, others may differ. Our administrative team will verify your specific benefits before treatment begins and provide you with a clear, written cost estimate. We also offer flexible financing options to help make treatment affordable. Call us at (817) 920-0882 to discuss your options.

faqs.q: What are the signs of gum disease I should watch for?
faqs.a: Watch for these warning signs of gum disease: gums that bleed when brushing or flossing; red, swollen, or tender gum tissue; persistent bad breath that doesn't resolve with brushing; gums that appear to be pulling away from your teeth (recession); loose or shifting teeth in adulthood; new spaces appearing between teeth; and pus between teeth and gums. Early gum disease (gingivitis) is often painless, which is why regular dental checkups are essential. If you notice any of these symptoms, call our Fort Worth office at (817) 920-0882 for an evaluation — don't wait.

faqs.q: What happens if gum disease is left untreated?
faqs.a: Untreated gum disease progresses steadily from gingivitis (reversible inflammation) through to severe periodontitis (irreversible bone and tissue destruction). The consequences include: tooth loss — the #1 cause of adult tooth loss in the US; jawbone loss — making future implants or dentures more complex; increased heart disease risk — gum bacteria enter the bloodstream; worsened diabetes control — the inflammation affects blood sugar; increased stroke risk — established by multiple large studies; and adverse pregnancy outcomes — linked to premature birth and low birth weight. Early treatment is always simpler, less expensive, and more effective. Schedule your evaluation today — don't let gum disease silently cause long-term damage.

faqs.q: Can gum disease come back after laser treatment?
faqs.a: Gum disease can recur if good oral hygiene and regular professional maintenance are not maintained. This is why post-treatment periodontal maintenance visits every 3–4 months are essential — they allow Dr. Brown to monitor your gum pocket depths, remove bacterial build-up before it re-infects the tissue, and keep your results lasting long-term. At home, consistent brushing twice daily, daily flossing, and using an antimicrobial mouthwash significantly reduces the risk of recurrence. Dr. Brown will provide you with a personalised home care plan after your treatment.
